newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court for charging opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: Indian court for charging opposition leader.

text.p: An Indian court on Friday ordered charges to be brought against a senior leader of the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party, the Press Trust of India reported.
L.K. Advani would be charged based on documentary evidence made available by the federal police for his alleged involvement in a bribe-for-favours scandal, judge V.B. Gupta ordered.
Advani is among some 100 politicians and bureacrats who have been named by an illlegal foreign exchange dealer as reciving bribes in exchange for political favours.

The $18 million scandal has forced seven ministers in the previous Congress government of P.V. Narasimha Rao to resign, and was widely seen as leading to the Congress party's defeat in the general elections in April/May this year.
The Central Bureau of Investigation in January accused Advani of receiving 350 million rupees as "illegal gratification" between March 1988 and April 1990.
Advani has been asked to appear before a special court on September 26 when charges will be formally brought against him.
Advani had denied all charges linked to the scandal although he has resigned from parliament.
The same court also recently ordered charges to be brought against V.C. Shukla, a minister in Rao's cabinet.
